g.text: C220 · §1.4.5 Monolithic vs multi-chip photonic–electronic integration

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Putting electronics right next to photonics → better performance, lower cost, new designs. Two ways to do it:

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 · Monolithic: one wafer, one process flow

g.text: Takeaway: monolithic = one flow (Luxtera 130 nm, Ge + Si etches added); multi-chip = best CMOS bonded to a cheap photonics wafer.

g.text: Photonics: ~100 nm features, large devices → economics tends to drive it into its own process; unmodified 45 nm SOI is not expected to compete.
